title: Chapter 101
content:
Jakyeong stared down at his blood-soaked clothes. The lacerations along both forearms had been stitched and wrapped in thick layers of gauze, making his arms look like a pair of mummified limbs. He remained frozen on the waiting room bench, staring blankly at the dried blood caked beneath his fingernails until Wang Ryun finally lost his patience.

"Head back to your room," Ryun urged, his voice heavy with concern. "Sitting out here in that state won't do anyone any good."

When Jakyeong didn't budge, Ryun reached down to haul him to his feet. Jakyeong dug his heels in, refusing to yield, prompting Wang Han to place a restraining hand on Ryun's shoulder with a quiet shake of his head. Ryun let out a long, defeated breath and turned around. Down the sterile corridor, a line of suited security operatives stood in rigid silence outside the surgical theater.

Park Tae-soo had been running on pure adrenaline, coordinating damage control the moment Il-hyun was wheeled into the trauma bay. As the hours stretched on, the operating room doors swung open intermittently, but each time Jakyeong sprang up from the bench, it was only surgical staff moving in and out with supplies.

Dr. Kang Yu-jung had scrubbed in as well. Trapped beneath a suffocating wave of guilt, Jakyeong found it impossible to look her in the eye.

Time ground to a grueling halt. Exhausted, Wang Han and Ryun eventually stepped away to the rooftop for a smoke, leaving Jakyeong rooted before the double doors, his eyes burning into the frosted glass panels.

A pair of measured footsteps echoed down the tile. Jakyeong looked up to find Park Tae-soo returning from his rounds.

"If you return to your suite to rest, Young Master, I will notify you the moment the operation concludes."

Though the offer was delivered with courteous deference, Jakyeong remained silent. A heavy tension lingered between them. Watching Tae-soo check the time, Jakyeong was the first to speak.

"What about... Chairman Kang?"

A deep, bone-weary exhaustion showed on Tae-soo's usually unflappable face.

"He remains unconscious as well."

Jakyeong’s expression darkened. The patriarch he had assumed dead had been rushed to the emergency wing, barely surviving the trauma through emergency neurosurgery. That wretched old monster. His grip on life was infuriatingly stubborn. Jakyeong cursed himself for not finishing the job right then and there.

Before the frustration could fester, the surgical doors parted again, and Jakyeong rose to his feet.

An orderly wheeled a gurney out into the corridor, revealing Kang Il-hyun.

His upper torso was swathed in heavy compression dressings, the hospital sheet drawn up to his broad shoulders. He was entirely unresponsive, an oxygen mask fogging with each mechanical breath. Suspended from an IV pole beside the gurney was an array of saline drips and blood transfusion bags, while his face remained as stark and drained of color as parchment.

Following close behind, Yu-jung pulled down her surgical mask, turning her tired gaze toward Tae-soo.

"He's being transferred to the intensive care unit. Tonight is the critical window. Even if he survives through the morning, we'll need to monitor him closely for the next several days."

Having delivered the prognosis, she turned to leave, but Jakyeong instinctively caught her sleeve. The crimson stains blooming across her surgical gown needed no explanation. Overwhelmed with shame, his fingers slid away from her fabric, his voice cracking into a ragged whisper.

"I am... so sorry..."

Instead of cold fury, she merely exhaled a quiet, melancholy breath.

"Go to your room and rest. Family visits aren't permitted right now anyway."

"Yes, ma'am..."

She hesitated for a brief second, offered a gentle pat against his shoulder, and disappeared down the long corridor.
Returning with takeout containers, Wang Han and Ryun found Jakyeong’s hospital room deserted and headed straight down to the intensive care ward.

Sure enough, Jakyeong was sitting outside the glass partition in his standard-issue patient gown, unmoving.

Resting his head back against the wall with his eyes closed, the exhaustion etched into his features was absolute. He had suffered significant blood loss himself, and the attending physician had ordered strict bed rest, yet he had maintained this relentless vigil for days on end.

"Are you going to keep this up?" Wang Han snapped, unable to watch the self-destruction any longer. "At this rate, you'll be in the morgue before Director Kang even wakes up."

Scabs had formed over the split skin of Jakyeong's lips and cheeks, and his face had grown hollow from skipping meals. Beneath dark lashes, his brown irises drifted open, blinking through the haze before shutting again. He offered no defense, sitting as motionless as carved stone.

The two brothers let out a shared sigh, taking the empty seats beside him.

Eventually, the afternoon visitation window opened. For the past two days, restricted access had been granted for one brief session per day—just enough time to confirm a pulse through the glass.

Jakyeong rose from the bench, donned a sterile gown and mask, and stepped through the airlock.

The unit was filled with the rhythmic hiss of ventilators keeping fragile lives tethered to the world, alongside the quiet rustle of nurses moving between stations. An attendant guided him to the isolation suite at the far end of the floor.

Lying in the center of the room, Il-hyun looked largely unchanged from the night he left surgery. His frame was slightly more gaunt, a shadow of dark stubble lining his sharp jaw, his breathing still driven by the machine.

Once the attendant stepped outside, Jakyeong pulled a chair to the bedside.

Bandages covered the breadth of Il-hyun's torso, faint blossoms of blood seeping through the white cotton. His cheek remained bruised, with a clean row of sutures closing the laceration at his temple. Jakyeong took in every detail, letting his gaze drift toward the IV port taped to the back of Il-hyun's hand before reaching out.

The moment his fingers brushed the warm skin, a hot, suffocating lump rose in his throat.

His vision blurred, the sting of unshed tears burning behind his eyes.

"Please... wake up."

The words slipped out in a rough, cracked whisper. It dawned on him that he had never once held this man's hand of his own volition.

At least the skin was warm.

Don't leave me behind. If you open your eyes, I'll do whatever you want. I'll let myself care for you. Just don't slip away into the dark... Please, just wake up.

He fought with everything he had to hold the tears back, but a hot drop spilled over his lashes, tracing a line down his cheek. Had the nurse not stepped in to signal the end of the visitation window, the dam might have broken completely.

Wiping his eyes against the gauze on his forearm, Jakyeong stepped out into the waiting area where Ryun, Wang Han, and Tae-soo stood watch.
[A full week has passed since Haewon Group Chairman Kang Hoon and CEO Kang Il-hyun were abducted and critically injured by unidentified assailants. Earlier this morning, Chairman Kang succumbed to his injuries while in intensive care. In response, prosecutors and the National Police Agency have classified the incident as a targeted act of corporate terrorism linked to an affiliated syndicate, vowing to mobilize all investigative resources to apprehend those responsible.]

The 24-hour news networks were dominated by coverage of the Haewon Group tragedy, with broadsheet headlines speculating on the succession vacuum left in Chairman Kang's wake. Online media outlets were already running unverified reports detailing the long-standing friction between father and son, framing the incident as an internal power struggle. Tabloids even began exhuming the circumstances surrounding Il-hyun's mother's death, turning the family's dark history into public fodder.

Watching the broadcast in the private suite, Wang Han frowned.

"Chairman Kang's sudden passing makes no sense. Clinically speaking, his vitals were far more stable than Director Kang's."

Ryun scoffed, waving a dismissive hand. "Who cares? Good riddance. If that old devil had regained consciousness first, our heads would be on pikes right now."

"True enough. I was debating whether I needed to sneak in and finish him off myself."

Hearing footsteps outside, Wang Han clicked the television off.

Jakyeong entered the suite with a cast supporting his fractured leg. Over a week had passed since the extraction. Though Il-hyun’s clinical markers had stabilized, he had yet to regain consciousness.

Jakyeong spending entire days anchored outside the intensive care unit had become a fixture of the ward. Eventually, the brothers, Dr. Kang, and even Tae-soo had surrendered to his stubbornness.

Jakyeong’s eyes fell upon the morning paper resting on the glass table. Wang Han moved to flip the page over, but Jakyeong had already heard the broadcast.

It was difficult to wrap his head around the news; according to Tae-soo's updates, the old man had been in far better condition than Il-hyun.

The door clicked open as Dr. Kang Yu-jung stepped inside.

She examined the healing lacerations along Jakyeong’s arms, cleaning the incisions with antiseptic before applying fresh gauze. Her touch was gentle and measured. To look at her, one would never guess she had lost her biological father only hours ago.

Jakyeong sat in uncomfortable silence. He was the one who had driven the axe into Chairman Kang's skull. Did she know the truth? If she did, could she still treat him with such quiet warmth?

Because she was the sole family member Il-hyun genuinely trusted, Jakyeong dreaded the thought of earning her hatred.

Securing the tape, she glanced up with a faint smile. "You're scheduled for discharge tomorrow, correct?"

"Yes, ma'am..."

"That's a relief. You have no idea how many complaints we've received from the nursing floor. Word spread that a remarkably handsome young man was lingering outside the ICU all day, and half the staff kept finding excuses to pass by."

She delivered the joke with an easy grin, then paused as her eyes caught the morning broadsheet on the table. Picking it up, she scanned the obituary detailing her father's death.

Wang Han and Ryun held their breath, carefully gauging her reaction.

Without a flicker of emotion, she tossed the paper straight into the wastebasket.

Slipping her hands into the pockets of her lab coat, she spoke with cool, detached indifference:

"People in this country are entirely too obsessed with other people's business. He lived his life, his time came, and he died. Isn't that all there is to it?"

The Wang brothers stood frozen, mouths slightly parted in disbelief. Jakyeong looked up, equally stunned.

Yu-jung offered a bright, pleasant smile. "Rest well tonight, and have a smooth discharge tomorrow."

When Jakyeong gave a quiet nod, she offered a polite farewell and stepped out into the hallway.

Jakyeong stared at the wastebasket where the broadsheet lay crumpled, Chairman Kang's portrait resting among the discarded medical wrappers.

Ryun tilted his head toward the closed door. "Is it just me, or does she share an uncanny resemblance to President Kang?"

Wang Han rubbed his chin, nodding slowly.

At first glance, she seemed nothing more than an accomplished, elegant surgeon, but beneath the surface lay the same chilling, impenetrable composure that defined her brother. Whether that ice was an inherited family trait remained something no outsider could ever truly decipher.
